text:
anya: Heads-up — noticed p95/p99 tail latency jump after we swinged back to the older queue policy around 01:20 UTC. Impacting a subset of small-chat traffic.

kevin: Confirmed on dashboards. p99 spiked from ~120ms -> ~420ms for the small-request slice. Throughput dropped ~10% during the window.

maria: Is this the change that reduced token_budget target and shortened batch timeout? I thought swingback was only gating behavior.

anya: It was a combined deploy: restored previous enqueue gating but also applied a conservative token_budget=32 override to reduce head-of-line blocking. The commit is r-infer/commit/ab12cd (deployed 01:17).

perf-ci-bot: regression alert: inference_p99_latency: +300ms (CI detect), affected model: redwood/small-chat-v1, traffic tag: small-reqs.

sam: Quick profiling snapshot from a hot pod during spike:
```
Flame summary (sampled):
- 58%: kernel_dispatch -> kernel_small_batch (launch overhead dominates)
- 23%: rq_queue_wait (short polling spin)
- 12%: kv_cache_miss_handler (async ioctl -> memcpy)
- 7%: cuda_memcpy (host->dev)
```
This smells like more small batches hitting the small-batch kernel; kernel selection cost + increased kv misses (less opportunity to reuse KV prefix)

kevin: That aligns with the queue instrumentation I pulled: batch_size histogram shifted left; median batch size went from 12 -> 3 for the affected tier. Also saw batch formation time fall but more single-request dispatches.

maria: Did kernel selector switch thresholds change? I recall we tightened the threshold that prefers fused-paths for >8 tokens.

anya: We didn't intentionally change kernel selector, but the selector uses observed batch size + seq_len distribution. Because batches are smaller, selector picks the 'low-latency' small-kernel which has higher per-token overhead for average seq_len 256.

sam: Also worth noting the token_budget reduction interacts: smaller token_budget caused early flushes for requests with uneven seq_len, reducing chance to coalesce prefixes in KV cache. KV cache hit rate for that window dropped ~18%.

kevin: Reproduced locally in perf harness by forcing token_budget=32 and enabling old enqueue gating. Repro script: `scripts/harness/repro_small_batches.sh --model small-chat-v1 --qpolicy swingback --token-budget 32`. Results: p99 ~410ms. With token_budget=64 and new gating p99 ~125ms.

anya: Stack traces show repeated kernel launch overhead from small-batch path. Example perf snippet:
```
# kernel dispatch latency samples
kernel_small_batch_launch: 140us (avg)
kernel_large_batch_fused: 28us (avg)
# mem copies per-request increased by ~1.2x
```
So aggregate latency stems from more frequent kernel launches + more memcpy due to KV misses.

maria: Proposed mitigations: 1) revert token_budget to 64 quickly; 2) bump batch_timeout_ms from 4->8 for small tier to allow coalescing; 3) add a temporary rule to prefer fused kernels when seq_len>128 even if batch_size<8. Any cons?

kevin: 1+2 low-risk. 3 is touchy — changing selector heuristics quickly can have side-effects on other workloads (latency-sensitive tiny-requests). But we can gate it to the small-chat model tag.

ops-bot: Revert candidate created: r-infer/reverts/r12345. Owner: @anya. Estimated rollout 5m.

anya: I'll push revert for token_budget and bump timeout now (will canary to us-east-1 small-chat pool).

(10m pass)

anya: Canary results: p99 back to ~140ms, KV hit rate improved by ~12%, throughput recovered. No other regressions observed on other tiers in canary.

sam: Follow-up profiling after revert: kernel_large_batch_fused regained 55% share, kernel_small_batch down to 18%, memcopy reduced.

kevin: Recording root cause: interaction effect — swingback of queue gating combined with an overly conservative token_budget produced a distribution of smaller batches that forced the kernel selector into a suboptimal code path, amplifying kernel launch overhead and increasing KV cache miss rate.

maria: Action items: 
- anya: keep token_budget=64 and batch_timeout_ms=8 for prod (done).
- kevin: add telemetry: emit selected_kernel name per-batch + batch formation reason tag (timeout vs budget vs capacity) — low effort, high signal.
- sam: add a regression test in perf harness that simulates mixed seq_len traffic to ensure kernel selector doesn't oscillate (test PR queued).
- infra: schedule a 24h roll monitor and alert if p99 rises >50ms from baseline.

anya: Will follow up with a short postmortem doc in #incidents later. Thanks for fast triage :thumbsup:

kevin: One more note — let's avoid flipping queue policies and token budget in the same deploy. Separate concerns next time.

maria: Agreed. Also plan a minor kernel-selector telemetry spike (sampling 1%) to capture seq_len vs batch size mapping in prod for 48h.

perf-ci-bot: closing regression alert (new baseline established after revert).

ops-bot: prod change rolled out to 3 regions at 02:03 UTC.

anya: Closing thread. Follow-up: will post postmortem link when available.
